title: Tragedy on the Pitch: 2 Dead, 11 Injured After Truck Drives Through Kansas Youth Soccer Game
snippet: A peaceful Saturday afternoon of youth soccer turned into a nightmare in Wichita, Kansas, after a truck drove onto a field, killing a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man.
content:
WICHITA, Kan. — What was supposed to be a joyful Saturday afternoon at the soccer field turned into a scene of unimaginable tragedy when a pickup truck drove through a youth match in Wichita, killing two people—including a 6-year-old boy—and injuring 11 others, authorities said.

First responders flooded the Stryker Sports Complex after frantic 911 calls began pouring in around 3:25 p.m. CT, according to Wichita Police Captain Aaron Moses. Upon arrival, officers located the vehicle on the west end of the field, where panic-stricken bystanders were already attempting to give life-saving first aid to the victims.

A Devastating Loss

Police confirmed that a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man, both from McPherson, Kansas, were pronounced dead at the scene. Eleven additional victims were rushed to nearby hospitals with traumatic injuries ranging from deep bruising to critical conditions.

Among the injured were five children between the ages of 5 and 9, as well as six adults ranging in age from 28 to 68.

Investigation and Heroic Response

Investigators identified the driver as a 34-year-old woman from Garden City, Kansas, who remained at the scene following the crash. Police said she had two juveniles inside her truck when she drove onto the field. While one of her own children was playing soccer at the complex that afternoon, officials clarified the child was on a different field at the time.

The driver was taken into custody and is cooperating with law enforcement. However, authorities emphasized that the investigation is still in its early stages as they attempt to determine what led to the crash.

"We know what happened, but now we're working very hard to find out why it happened, and we're not there yet," Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan told reporters during a press conference. Chief Sullivan praised the crowd for stepping up in the immediate aftermath, commending community members who "sprang into action so quickly and gave life-saving assistance until the arrival of first responders."

Community in Mourning

Local leaders expressed heartbreak as the city grappled with the horrific event. Wichita Mayor Lily Wu noted that families had gathered simply to enjoy watching their kids play sports before tragedy struck.

"Tonight, Wichita grieves together," Mayor Wu said. "No one could have imagined the tragedy that would unfold."

All remaining events at the Stryker Sports Complex have been canceled indefinitely. Officials are asking anyone who witnessed the incident or has video footage to contact the Wichita Police Department as investigators continue to interview witnesses.
